headline: The forecast goes live
body: Thirty-three forecast lines across seven domains, 2026 to 2200, written on 22 October 2026. From here on, a weekly check-in reads the news against the leading indicators and revises lines in public. Every revision is logged here with its reason.

headline: Four world-state paths now split at the hinge
body: Life expectancy, average paid hours, AI share of cognitive work and the off-Earth population now follow separate paths under pluralism and concentration instead of one shared path. Under concentration, aging therapies reach fewer people (median life expectancy in 2100: 99 vs 115), paid hours fall faster and mostly involuntarily (5 vs 8 a week in 2100), and a single dominant actor builds faster off-Earth (150k vs 50k people in 2100). Population and warming stay shared. No event probabilities moved.

headline: The forecast becomes a film
body: The site now opens on a scroll-driven film of the century. The planet is drawn from the forecast itself: city lights track population, the atmosphere tracks warming, the web of links tracks AI's share of cognitive work and collapses into one hub if concentration wins, orbiting lights track the off-Earth population, and the red arc tracks the Doomsday Clock. Play runs about 90 seconds and holds on each cornerstone. No forecast numbers changed.

headline: One idea per screen
body: Every event now carries a hero figure (its own number or phrase) and one planet effect, and the film shows one idea per screen: the year, one stat, the hero figure, the title. Chapter openers are full-screen title cards. The 2039 fork shows two planets side by side to choose between. The ending counts up the flourish odds for the chosen branch. No forecast numbers changed; the hero fields restate figures already in the lines.
